summary: Dual-thumb range filter over a dithered histogram; bars inside the range light up and a result count follows as you drag or type.

attributes.name: min
attributes.description: Lower bound of the scale. Observed.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: Upper bound of the scale. Observed.

attributes.name: step
attributes.description: Snap increment, counted from `min`. Also the arrow-key step and the minimum gap between the two thumbs. Values at or below 0 fall back to 5. Observed.

attributes.name: low
attributes.description: Lower value. Defaults to `min` plus 20% of the range, snapped to `step`. Observed: a change moves the thumb without firing events.

attributes.name: high
attributes.description: Upper value. Defaults to `min` plus 70% of the range, snapped to `step`. Observed: a change moves the thumb without firing events.

attributes.name: prefix
attributes.description: Text before values in the Min and Max fields and in `aria-valuetext`. An empty attribute removes it. Observed.

attributes.name: data
attributes.description: Comma-separated bar heights for the histogram, spread evenly from `min` to `max`. Needs at least four numbers; otherwise a built-in demo distribution of 44 bars is used. Observed.

attributes.name: scale
attributes.description: Multiplier from the summed heights of the bars in range to the result count in the header. Observed.

attributes.name: unit-label
attributes.description: Word after the result count. Observed.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Form field name. With a name, the form receives `<name>-min` and `<name>-max`.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Presence attribute. Disables both thumbs and fields; a disabled ancestor `<fieldset>` does the same.

events.name: input
events.description: Fires on every value change by the user: while dragging, on key presses and when a Min or Max field is committed. Not fired for attribute changes.

events.name: change
events.description: Fires when a drag ends, after an arrow, Page, Home or End key press that moved a thumb, and when a Min or Max field is committed with a new value.

properties.name: bins
properties.description: The histogram bar heights in use, from `data` or the demo distribution.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The `name` attribute. There is no setter; set the attribute instead.

keyboard.action: Move the focused thumb by a tenth of the range.
Move the focused thumb to `min` or `max`, stopping one `step` from the other thumb.

accessibility: Both thumbs are focusable with `role="slider"`, `aria-label` `Minimum` or `Maximum`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and an `aria-valuetext` that includes the prefix.
The Min and Max text fields carry matching `aria-label`s and `inputmode="numeric"`.
The result count is an `aria-live="polite"` region.
Pressing on the track moves and focuses the nearest thumb. The histogram canvas is `aria-hidden`.
motion: With reduced motion, histogram bars switch between lit and unlit at once and the result count changes without the roll; the thumb glow still eases.
form: With `name`, submits two entries, `<name>-min` and `<name>-max`; without a name the internal value is `low-high`. There is no validation. Form reset restores the range from the first connect; `disabled` or a disabled fieldset takes the thumbs and fields out of use.
notes: The host is `display: block`; the plot is 118px tall and fills the host's width.
All attributes are observed: new bounds, a new `step` or new `data` re-clamp the thumbs and recount without events. The thumbs always stay at least one `step` apart.
A Min or Max field always shows the value in use after it is committed, also when the typed value was invalid or out of range.
There is no `value` property; read the range from the `input` and `change` details or from the form data.
The Min and Max fields' native `input` events stay inside the shadow root; only the element's own `input` and `change` events, with `min` and `max` in `detail`, reach the host.

data.note: Pass your histogram as `data` and the count factor as `scale`. Without `data` the histogram is a generated demo distribution.
